## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (the two `record()` call sites around the structured and agentic run paths) reads `req.target.get("ticket_id")` when building the usage-log row, but every producer of `target` writes the plural key `ticket_ids` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` and `src/rebar/llm/operations.py`). Result: 0 of the ~11,900 rows in `.rebar/usage.jsonl` carry a ticket, so per-ticket (and therefore per-review) cost attribution from the usage log is impossible, and `docs/llm-framework.md`'s claim that rows carry `ticket` is false. The eval ledger needs per-run attribution and this is the cheapest fix on that path.

## Approach

Read `ticket_ids` (first element, or the joined list) at both call sites, keep accepting the singular key for compatibility, and correct the doc sentence. Do not change the producers' key.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`
- `docs/llm-framework.md`
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` (or the existing runner usage test)

## Testing

Unit: a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[id]` yields a usage row with `ticket == id`; one carrying the legacy singular key still works; one with neither yields `ticket=None`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New usage-log rows produced by a gate session carry the ticket id; checked by running one `review-plan` locally (or the Tier-1 commissioning run) and inspecting the rows.
- [ ] The regression test above passes in `make test`.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` describes the actual field.
